pool.text: Points \( A, B, C, D \) lie on a circle. Chords \( AC \) and \( BD \) intersect at \( X \). If angle \( \angle ABD = 42^\circ \), what is the size of angle \( \angle ACD \)?
pool.sol: Angles in the same segment subtended by the same arc \( AD \) are equal. Therefore, \( \angle ACD = \angle ABD = 42^\circ \). [B1]
pool.q: Points \( A, B, C, D \) lie on a circle. Chords \( AC \) and \( BD \) intersect at \( X \). If angle \( \angle ABD = 42^\circ \), what is the size of angle \( \angle ACD \)?

pool.text: A line \( TA \) is tangent to a circle at \( A \). \( ABC \) is a triangle inscribed in the circle. If angle \( \angle TAB = 52^\circ \), what is the size of angle \( \angle ACB \)?
pool.sol: By the Alternate Segment Theorem, the angle between a tangent and a chord is equal to the angle subtended by the chord in the alternate segment: \( \angle ACB = \angle TAB = 52^\circ \). [B1]
pool.q: A line \( TA \) is tangent to a circle at \( A \). \( ABC \) is a triangle inscribed in the circle. If angle \( \angle TAB = 52^\circ \), what is the size of angle \( \angle ACB \)?

pool.text: Points \( P, Q, R \) lie on a circle with centre \( O \). Tangents from external point \( T \) touch the circle at \( P \) and \( Q \). If angle \( \angle PTQ = 46^\circ \), what is the size of angle \( \angle PRQ \) on the major arc?
pool.sol: In quadrilateral \( OPTQ \), angles \( \angle OPT = \angle OQT = 90^\circ \) (tangents perpendicular to radius). The opposite angles sum to \( 180^\circ \): \( \angle POQ = 180^\circ - 46^\circ = 134^\circ \). The angle at the circumference \( \angle PRQ \) is half the angle at the centre: \( \angle PRQ = \dfrac{134^\circ}{2} = 67^\circ \). [M1 for finding angle POQ = 134, M1 for dividing by 2, A1 for 67]
pool.q: Points \( P, Q, R \) lie on a circle with centre \( O \). Tangents from external point \( T \) touch the circle at \( P \) and \( Q \). If angle \( \angle PTQ = 46^\circ \), what is the size of angle \( \angle PRQ \) on the major arc?

pool.text: In a cyclic quadrilateral \( ABCD \), \( AB \) is extended to point \( E \). If angle \( \angle CBE = 74^\circ \), what is the size of interior angle \( \angle ADC \)?
pool.sol: Angles on a straight line: \( \angle ABC = 180^\circ - 74^\circ = 106^\circ \). In cyclic quadrilateral \( ABCD \), opposite angles sum to \( 180^\circ \): \( \angle ADC = 180^\circ - \angle ABC = 180^\circ - 106^\circ = 74^\circ \). (The exterior angle of a cyclic quad equals the opposite interior angle). [M1 for straight line or exterior angle theorem, A1 for 74]
pool.q: In a cyclic quadrilateral \( ABCD \), \( AB \) is extended to point \( E \). If angle \( \angle CBE = 74^\circ \), what is the size of interior angle \( \angle ADC \)?

pool.q: In a regular polygon, each exterior angle is 24°. How many sides does the polygon have?
pool.text: In a regular polygon, each exterior angle is 24°. How many sides does the polygon have?
pool.sol: Number of sides = \( \frac{360^\circ}{\text{exterior angle}} = \frac{360^\circ}{24^\circ} = 15 \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: The interior angle of a regular polygon is 160°. How many sides does the polygon have?
pool.text: The interior angle of a regular polygon is 160°. How many sides does the polygon have?
pool.sol: Exterior angle = \( 180^\circ - 160^\circ = 20^\circ \). Number of sides = \( \frac{360^\circ}{20^\circ} = 18 \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: Two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal. One of the co-interior angles is 68°. What is the other co-interior angle?
pool.text: Two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal. One of the co-interior angles is 68°. What is the other co-interior angle?
pool.sol: Co-interior angles sum to \( 180^\circ \): \( 180^\circ - 68^\circ = 112^\circ \). [B1]

pool.q: Triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle such that AB is a diameter. If angle BAC = 34°, find the size of angle ABC.
pool.text: Triangle ABC is inscribed in a circle such that AB is a diameter. If angle BAC = 34°, find the size of angle ABC.
pool.sol: Angle in a semicircle is \( 90^\circ \) (\( \angle ACB = 90^\circ \)). \( \angle ABC = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 34^\circ = 56^\circ \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: In a circle, chords AB and CD intersect at point P. If angle ACD = 28°, what is the size of angle ABD?
pool.text: In a circle, chords AB and CD intersect at point P. If angle ACD = 28°, what is the size of angle ABD?
pool.sol: Angles in the same segment subtended by the same arc are equal: \( \angle ABD = \angle ACD = 28^\circ \). [B1]

pool.q: Two tangents TP and TQ are drawn from an external point T to a circle with centre O. If angle PTQ = 50°, find angle TPQ.
pool.text: Two tangents TP and TQ are drawn from an external point T to a circle with centre O. If angle PTQ = 50°, find angle TPQ.
pool.sol: Tangent lengths from a common external point are equal (\( TP = TQ \)). Triangle TPQ is isosceles with vertex angle 50°: \( \angle TPQ = \frac{180^\circ - 50^\circ}{2} = 65^\circ \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: A chord of length 24 cm is at a distance of 5 cm from the centre of a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
pool.text: A chord of length 24 cm is at a distance of 5 cm from the centre of a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
pool.sol: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord: half length = 12 cm. Radius = \( \sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13 \text{ cm} \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: A circle has radius 17 cm. A chord has length 30 cm. What is the perpendicular distance from the centre of the circle to the chord?
pool.text: A circle has radius 17 cm. A chord has length 30 cm. What is the perpendicular distance from the centre of the circle to the chord?
pool.sol: Half chord = 15 cm. Distance = \( \sqrt{17^2 - 15^2} = \sqrt{289 - 225} = \sqrt{64} = 8 \text{ cm} \). [M1 A1]

pool.q: In cyclic quadrilateral PQRS, angle PQR = 104°. What is the size of the opposite angle PSR?
pool.text: In cyclic quadrilateral PQRS, angle PQR = 104°. What is the size of the opposite angle PSR?
pool.sol: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to \( 180^\circ \): \( \angle PSR = 180^\circ - 104^\circ = 76^\circ \). [B1]

pool.q: Points A, B, and C lie on a circle. Angle ABC = 47°. What is the reflex angle AOC subtended at centre O?

pool.text: A bank account pays compound interest of 3% per year. How many complete years will it take for an initial deposit of $2000 to exceed \$3000?
pool.sol: We need \( 2000(1.03)^n > 3000 \implies (1.03)^n > 1.5 \). Taking logarithms: \( n \ln(1.03) > \ln(1.5) \implies n > \dfrac{\ln(1.5)}{\ln(1.03)} \approx \dfrac{0.405465}{0.029559} \approx 13.72 \). The minimum number of complete years is 14. [M1 for setting up inequality, A1 for 14 years]
pool.q: A bank account pays compound interest of 3% per year. How many complete years will it take for an initial deposit of $2000 to exceed \$3000?

pool.text: A bag contains 6 green counters and 4 yellow counters. A counter is chosen at random, its colour recorded, and it is REPLACED. A second counter is then chosen. What is the probability that both counters are the same colour?
pool.sol:
Since the counter is replaced, events are independent:
\[ P(\text{Green, Green}) = \left(\dfrac{6}{10}\right)^2 = \dfrac{36}{100} \]
\[ P(\text{Yellow, Yellow}) = \left(\dfrac{4}{10}\right)^2 = \dfrac{16}{100} \]
\[ P(\text{Same Colour}) = \dfrac{36}{100} + \dfrac{16}{100} = \dfrac{52}{100} = \dfrac{13}{25}. \]

pool.text: A bag contains \( n \) marbles, of which 4 are green. Two marbles are taken at random without replacement. If the probability that both are green is \( \dfrac{2}{15} \), find the total number of marbles \( n \).
pool.sol: \( P(\text{both green}) = \dfrac{4}{n} \times \dfrac{3}{n - 1} = \dfrac{12}{n(n - 1)} \). Set equal to \( \dfrac{2}{15} \): \( \dfrac{12}{n(n - 1)} = \dfrac{2}{15} \implies 2n(n - 1) = 180 \implies n(n - 1) = 90 \implies n^2 - n - 90 = 0 \implies (n - 10)(n + 9) = 0 \). Since \( n > 0 \), \( n = 10 \). [M1 for setting up probability equation, M1 for quadratic n(n-1)=90, A1 for 10]
pool.q: A bag contains \( n \) marbles, of which 4 are green. Two marbles are taken at random without replacement. If the probability that both are green is \( \dfrac{2}{15} \), find the total number of marbles \( n \).

pool.text: A drawer contains 5 blue socks, 4 grey socks, and 3 black socks. Two socks are pulled at random without replacement. What is the probability of pulling two socks of different colours?
pool.sol:
Total socks = 12. Total pairs = \( \binom{12}{2} = 66 \).
Number of same-colour pairs:
\[ \binom{5}{2} + \binom{4}{2} + \binom{3}{2} = 10 + 6 + 3 = 19. \]
Therefore, the probability that the two socks have different colours is:
\[ P(\text{Different}) = 1 - \dfrac{19}{66} = \dfrac{47}{66}. \]
Sum=50, n=5, mean=10.

pool.text: In a class of 30 students, 18 study French (\(F\)), 15 study German (\(G\)), and 7 study both French and German. How many students study neither French nor German?

pool.text: Set \( A \) has 12 elements and set \( B \) has 8 elements. If \( A \cap B \neq \emptyset \), what is the maximum possible number of elements in \( A \cup B \)?
pool.sol: Formula: \( n(A \cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B) = 12 + 8 - n(A \cap B) = 20 - n(A \cap B) \). To maximize the union, we must minimize the intersection. Since \( A \cap B \neq \emptyset \), the minimum possible value of \( n(A \cap B) \) is 1. Thus maximum \( n(A \cup B) = 20 - 1 = 19 \). [M1 for maximizing union by minimizing intersection to 1, A1 for 19]

pool.text: A cuboid has length 10 cm, width 6 cm, and height 4 cm. Calculate the angle that the space diagonal makes with the base of the cuboid.
pool.sol: Diagonal of base: \( d_{\text{base}} = \sqrt{10^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{100 + 36} = \sqrt{136} \approx 11.66 \) cm. The vertical height is 4 cm. The angle \( \theta \) with the base satisfies \( \tan\theta = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{136}} \approx \dfrac{4}{11.6619} \approx 0.3430 \implies \theta = \tan^{-1}(0.3430) \approx 18.9^\circ \). [M1 for base diagonal sqrt(136), M1 for tan(theta)=4/sqrt(136), A1 for 18.9 (or 18.8)]
pool.q: A cuboid has length 10 cm, width 6 cm, and height 4 cm. Calculate the angle that the space diagonal makes with the base of the cuboid.

Acute angle = \( \sin^{-1}(0.5143) \approx 30.9^\circ \). The obtuse angle is \( 180^\circ - 30.9^\circ = 149.1^\circ \). [M1 for sine rule, M1 for 180 - acute, A1 for 149.1]
pool.q: In triangle \( ABC \), \( AB = 8 \) cm, \( BC = 11 \) cm, and angle \( BAC = 45^\circ \). Find the obtuse angle \( \angle ACB \) to 1 decimal place.
